2103.10385v2.pdf.title: GPT Understands, Too
2103.10385v2.pdf.one_sentence_summary: P-Tuning is a novel method that employs trainable continuous prompt embeddings to stabilize training and improve performance on various natural language understanding tasks, addressing the instability of manual discrete prompts.

2004.13845v1.pdf.title: DARE: Data Augmented Relation Extraction with GPT-2
2004.13845v1.pdf.one_sentence_summary: This work introduces DARE, a method using fine-tuned GPT-2 to generate augmented training data for Relation Extraction, effectively addressing limited data and class imbalance for BERT-based classifiers and achieving state-of-the-art results on biomedical datasets.

2102.08036v1.pdf.title: Exploring Transformers in Natural Language Generation: GPT, BERT, and XLNet
2102.08036v1.pdf.one_sentence_summary: This paper explores three major Transformer-based models—GPT, BERT, and XLNet—highlighting their advancements and significant implications for the field of Natural Language Generation by overcoming limitations of prior architectures.

2104.04466v3.pdf.title: Knowledge-Aware Graph-Enhanced GPT-2 for Dialogue State Tracking
2104.04466v3.pdf.one_sentence_summary: This paper presents a novel hybrid architecture that augments GPT-2 with Graph Attention Network representations to improve dialogue state tracking performance, particularly in capturing inter-slot dependencies and robustness under sparse supervision.

2003.01473v2.pdf.title: XGPT: Cross-modal Generative Pre-Training for Image Captioning
2003.01473v2.pdf.one_sentence_summary: XGPT introduces a novel cross-modal generative pre-training method for image captioning, utilizing an encoder-decoder architecture and three new generation tasks to achieve state-of-the-art results and improve understanding tasks like image retrieval.

2006.01997v1.pdf.title: Automatic Text Summarization of COVID-19 Medical Research Articles using BERT and GPT-2
2006.01997v1.pdf.one_sentence_summary: This work leverages pre-trained BERT and GPT-2 models for automatic abstractive and extractive text summarization of COVID-19 medical literature, providing succinct summaries to aid the medical community in managing the rapidly growing research.

2005.09123v2.pdf.title: GPT-too: A language-model-ﬁrst approach for AMR-to-text generation
2005.09123v2.pdf.one_sentence_summary: This paper proposes an AMR-to-text generation approach combining a pre-trained GPT-2 language model with cycle consistency-based re-scoring, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on the LDC2017T10 dataset through automatic and human evaluations.

2102.05126v3.pdf.title: AuGPT: Auxiliary Tasks and Data Augmentation for End-To-End Dialogue with Pre-Trained Language Models
2102.05126v3.pdf.one_sentence_summary: This paper introduces AuGPT, an end-to-end dialogue model based on GPT-2, which utilizes modified training objectives including a novel dialogue consistency classification task, token unlikelihood loss, and massive data augmentation via back-translation to improve performance and diversity in multi-domain task-oriented dialogue on the MultiWOZ dataset.

2003.02498v1.pdf.title: RecipeGPT: Generative Pre-training Based Cooking Recipe Generation and Evaluation System
2003.02498v1.pdf.one_sentence_summary: RecipeGPT is a novel online system for generating and evaluating cooking recipes, leveraging a fine-tuned GPT-2 model for both instruction and ingredient generation, and providing tools for user evaluation and comparison with reference recipes.

2006.15437v1.pdf.title: GPT-GNN: Generative Pre-Training of Graph Neural Networks
2006.15437v1.pdf.one_sentence_summary: GPT-GNN is a generative pre-training framework for Graph Neural Networks that uses a self-supervised attributed graph generation task to capture structural and semantic graph properties, enabling improved performance on downstream tasks with limited labeled data.

2007.00659v2.pdf.title: LSTM and GPT-2 Synthetic Speech Transfer Learning for Speaker Recognition to Overcome Data Scarcity
2007.00659v2.pdf.one_sentence_summary: This work addresses data scarcity in speaker recognition by generating synthetic Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) using LSTM and GPT-2 models, demonstrating that transfer learning with this synthetic data significantly improves speaker classification performance with limited real user data.
